Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. Acyphor is running the SIG questionnaire for Greenline Financial and we need a compact evidence bundle describing Redwood's secure software development lifecycle focusing on: code review / PR gating, CI/CD controls (runners, ephemeral creds), secrets management and rotation, and change management approvals.

Specifically we need the following items (single reply with all attachments/links is fine):
- PR gating policy (required checks, branch protection, label->workflow mapping)
- Example merged PR showing review history and automated gating logs (redacted as needed)
- CI runner configuration and evidence of ephemeral credential usage + rotation schedule
- Secrets access matrix and KMS integration proof (samples or screenshots)
- Change approval audit sample (approver list, timestamps, rollout note)
- A short narrative (one page) explaining how rollbacks/fallbacks are authorized under emergency patching.

Timeline: Greenline would like these by end of day Friday (2026-05-28) to keep the assessment on track. If anything is sensitive we can accept redacted artifacts and a short attestation.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that makes coordination easier.

Regards,
Emma Roth
Senior Assessor, Acyphor Risk

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. Looping in Jordan (DevOps) for CI/runner artifacts and Lauren (Security) for PR gating + change approvals. We can meet the Friday EOD ask and will include redacted samples where appropriate.

High-level notes up front:
- PR gating: branch protection + required reviews + automated checks (lint, unit, integration, security scans). We map PR labels (e.g., "infra/patch", "feature", "secfix") to specific pipeline workflows; I will attach the policy doc and a mapping table.
- CI/CD: we run self-hosted runners in our VPC and use short-lived tokens for pipeline steps. Runners obtain ephemeral vault tokens via OIDC to fetch secrets; rotation policy is enforced at the vault layer with a 30-day default and shorter windows for high-risk keys.
- Secrets: primary KMS is AWS KMS with a HSM-backed key for production keystore. Access matrix and sample audit logs will be attached (redacted).
- Change approvals: rollouts are gated by an approval pipeline that requires two approvers for non-trivial changes and auto-fallback to previous stable canary if health checks fail; I'll include a sample approval audit log.

Attachments we will provide in the next email: pr-gating-policy-v2.pdf, ci-runner-ephemeral-rotation.csv, secrets-access-matrix.xlsx, change-approval-audit-sample.log. Also linking a short narrative and playbook in Drive.

If you prefer a call I can do Thu 14:00-15:00 ET or Fri 11:00-12:00 ET.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Emma —

Attached is the requested bundle and a short narrative. Notes below and pointers to the Drive folder.

Quick answers:
- OIDC / runner ephemerality: runners use short-lived OIDC assertions (TTL 5 minutes) to request Vault tokens. Runners are ephemeral by default (image-boot on demand via autoscaling); we rotate images weekly for base dependencies and have an immutable artifact hash. See attached "ci-runner-ephemeral-rotation.csv" for sample token_request_time / ttl entries (redacted UIDs).
- Rotation SLOs: high-privilege KMS keys — annual rotation with emergency rotation procedure; application secrets (API keys, DB credentials) — default 30 days; service tokens used by internal pipelines — 7 days. Custodians are listed in the attached "secrets-access-matrix.xlsx".
- PR example: included zipped PR export (metadata only) showing the label "secfix", required reviewers, automated security scanner blocking merge until SARIF compliance check passed. File: pr-gating-policy-v2.pdf includes the label->workflow mapping table.
- Change approvals: attached audit log excerpt "change-approval-audit-sample.log" shows approver ids and timestamps; non-trivial changes require two approvers and an automated canary health gate. Emergency patches can be escalated via an on-call approval path (described in the narrative).

Drive folder (view only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xq-sample-docs-Redwood
Internal reference playbook: https://redwood-internal.company/docs/ci-runner-ops-playbook

If you want to review live artifacts we can provide screen-shared walkthroughs during the 30-minute call. I booked Fri 11:00-11:30 ET on your calendar (invite sent).

Regards,
Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference
